title: Four thousand, one
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday. Wood keeps a tally of cuts on the backroom wall in pencil: 'do four thousand.' He's at sixty-one. The owner sees the tally and adds a mark of her own. Sixty-two. She says that one's hers.

panels.composition: The backroom wall by the mat cutter: pencil tally marks in fives, and a heading in the display face: 4000. Sixty-one marks.

image.prompt: close on a wall beside a mat cutter with pencil tally marks in groups of five under a hand-lettered number, black and white, no words
image.notes: Letter after: 4000 (the heading); the tally as marks.

panels.composition: WOOD cutting. The OWNER passing behind him. Stopping at the wall. A pencil from behind her ear.

image.prompt: a young man cutting a mat while a woman in reading glasses pauses at a tally on the wall behind him and takes a pencil from behind her ear, black and white, no words
close on a woman's hand adding one pencil tally mark to a wall, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood turning. The owner already gone. The mark. He doesn't erase it.

image.prompt: a young man turning from a mat cutter to look at a fresh tally mark on the wall, the room empty behind him, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Sixty-two. One is hers. He doesn't erase it.
